terms.gloss: an idea of something, a notion, a concept
evidence: Cic. Top. 31: nōtiōnem appellō, quod Graecī tum ἔννοιαν tum πρόληψιν dīcunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for Greek ἔννοια: nōtiō virī bonī, the idea of a good man (Off. 3.81).

terms.gloss: a thought, something that occurs to one
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.51: multō difficilior occurrit cōgitātiō, multō obscūrior, quālis animus in corpore sit

terms.gloss: an idea that something is so, a belief, an impression
evidence: Caes. BG 3.17: tantamque opīniōnem timōris praebuit, and gave such an impression of fear

terms.comment: Properly “getting to know, knowledge”; in Cicero also the idea formed in the mind.

phrases.english: “What sort?” you ask. I have no idea: it was called a tragedy.

phrases.latin: quod in omnium animīs eōrum nōtiōnem inpressisset ipsa nātūra
phrases.english: because nature herself had stamped an idea of them on every mind

sources: Lewis & Short: notio · Lewis & Short: cogitatio · Lewis & Short: opinio
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. idea.
